The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for shoppers
Why, in plain words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary made account pages fail for shoppers, likely because the summary divides by the number of items bought this month and some shoppers had bought nothing this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,422.30 USD {customer_loss}
- People who responded: 2 {responders}
- Their time, added together: 17 min {engineer_minutes}

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #578 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for shoppers while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 19:28 to 19:36 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 19:53:20 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 19:34:52 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 19:28 UTC and was back to normal at 19:36 UTC, 8 minutes later. 29.9% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,422.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching on a new monthly spending summary made account pages fail for shoppers, likely because the summary divides by the number of items bought this month and some shoppers had bought nothing this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #578, for a person to review and merge. Turning monthly-spend-feature back on could make account pages fail again as they did here.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
2,868 - requests failed
0.9% to 29.9% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,422.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the month's spend by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division at line 47 raises ZeroDivisionError, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns each error into a failed account page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 37 minutes, 18:58–19:34; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:31
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:28–19:34
why 1 Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appears in the onset minute, and the logs read from before it show no such error.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 occurrences in 30 minutes, 18:58–19:27
why 2 Account page requests started taking the new spend-summary path when admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at 19:28:31 UTC. The flag's evaluations split between off and on during that minute and were all on in every minute after it.
  Evidence:
    P1 19:28:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 19:28
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 19:29–19:34
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 18:58–19:27
  Ruled out:
    A deploy: none came back for the day read before the onset. The revision running on every replica stayed in place after the flag was turned off, and the service went back to normal.
      T8 19:35:13 Investigator Agent: Read back 1 production change
      T9 19:35:13 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
      T18 19:37:09 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 19:36
      T19 19:37:10 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    The ClientDisconnected failures on account pages (shoppers closing the connection): these were already in the logs before the flag change, while account pages rendered normally.
      G46bc
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 26 minutes, 18:59–19:24
why 3 With the flag on, the spend summary likely computes a this-month average per item that cannot be computed for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- Before the flag could be switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the monthly spend path with the flag on for a shopper with no purchases this month. (AI-3)
- The flag went from off to on for all shoppers at once. No staged rollout or error-rate guard tied to the flag change was seen. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 19:28:31 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to 20-40%. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 19:28:31 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 19:35:30 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 19:38:52 | Proposed a fix: PR #578 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 19:28 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 19:34:27 UTC, 6 minutes 27 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #578 | open
AI-3 | Require the tests for any flag-gated code path to run with the flag on as well as off, and block switching the flag on in production until they pass. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Switch flags such as monthly-spend-feature on in stages, starting with a small share of shoppers, and hold each stage while the account page error rate is watched. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix proposed in PR #578, or another fix, has been reviewed and merged. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 48 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 1 minute 3 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 2 minutes 43 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 25 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #578.
- The log lines showed the flag's evaluations splitting between off and on in the minute the errors began, which tied the errors to the flag change directly.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 12 19:28 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 19:34:27 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 19:34:48 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 19:34:51 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 19:35:04 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 19:34:27
T4 | 19:35:09 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 361 minutes of metrics
T5 | 19:35:11 |  | Investigator Agent Placed the start of the incident at 19:28
T6 | 19:35:11 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 19:35:12 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 19:29
T8 | 19:35:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 1 production change
T9 | 19:35:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 19:35:13 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 minutes 27 seconds before 19:34:27
T11 | 19:35:13 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 124 log lines
T12 | 19:35:15 |  | Investigator Agent Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1
T13 | 19:35:15 |  | Investigator Agent Read every channel available
T14 | 19:35:15 |  | Argus Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 19:35:15

T16 | 19:35:30 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
T17 | 19:35:37 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 19:36 - up to 149s
 | 19:36 | IMPACT ENDS | the service was back to normal
T18 | 19:37:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 19:36
T19 | 19:37:10 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T20 | 19:37:10 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag monthly-spend-feature OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
T21 | 19:38:52 |  | Code-Fix Agent Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #578

Response effort
17 min - engineer time, 2 responders
144,914 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/43fcd97c-a472-43ff-80b3-09c598d198ec
The fix it proposed: PR #578 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/578) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 19:28:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 18:58–19:27
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 36 occurrences in 30 minutes, 18:58–19:27
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 occurrences in 37 minutes, 18:58–19:34; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:31
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 occurrences in 26 minutes, 18:59–19:24
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 19:28
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:28–19:34
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 19:29–19:34
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month), where bought_this_month is the purchases flagged in_current_month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list there, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError. That is not an edge case. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, render_spend_summary never reached this function. With it on, every such shopper's request reached it, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each error into a failed page.

The change: if there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0. Nothing was spent per item this month, and total_this_month_cents is itself 0 for such an account in the fixtures. Otherwise the division is unchanged. With the flag off, nothing changes. average_spend_per_item and the lifetime path are untouched. They still raise for an account that has never bought anything, which the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py rely on. render_spend_summary and serve_account_page still get an int, so their return types and callers are unchanged.

The tests: three new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. Two call the monthly figure directly and through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper with no purchases this month, and expect 0. One expects 0 for a shopper with no history at all when the monthly flag is on. Each of these would raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. The test that expects a failure to reach the caller on the lifetime path stays as it is.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed for some shoppers. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. The trouble began when a new monthly spending summary was switched on. The likely reason is that the summary divides by the number of items a shopper bought this month, and some shoppers had bought nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. {responders} people responded and spent {engineer_minutes} of their time in total. To end the incident, Argus switched the new summary back off by reverting the monthly-spend-feature flag. The revert is confirmed and still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix to the summary, but it is only a draft and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
